fields.description:
## Problem

`infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/handler.py` prices CloudWatch token counts
using a rate table derived daily from Cost Explorer and matched to models by
string heuristics. That layer produced four defects in the twelve days since the
cap was deployed (2026-09-12):

1. `_rate_for`/`_match` direction-suffix collision: candidate suffix
   `input-token-count` also matches `...-cache-write-input-token-count` and the
   longest match wins, so a model's input rate resolves to its cache-write rate.
   Fires iff the ModelId has no version suffix — live for `claude-sonnet-4-6`,
   `claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-opus-5`.
2. `_normalise` mismatch: label `Nova2.0Lite` gives `nova20lite`, model id
   `us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0` gives `nova2litev10`; neither contains the other,
   so a rate already in the table is missed and the model falls to
   `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K`, set far above any real rate.
3. `BEDROCK_SERVICE_VALUES`, the hardcoded CE service allowlist from
   3083-ada3-3a0f-4051, omits five live Bedrock services, so the authoritative CE
   signal sees about a third of real spend.
4. `MARKETPLACE_TOKEN_SUFFIXES` handles only CamelCase usage types; AWS also
   bills snake_case (`USE1_input_tokens_standard-Units`) and `_Global` variants,
   which `_refresh_rates` skips silently.

Two reached production unalarmed: a model priced at the fail-closed fallback rate
for seven days, emitting 6,112 `fail-closed fallback` log events; and the
marketplace-units defect fixed by Gerrit 3032, where the estimate was five orders
of magnitude high. These are one class — matching model identifiers to billing
labels by substring and suffix — and four shapes have already occurred.

## Approach

Delete the pricing-derivation layer. Price every token at a ceiling rate for its
direction, set above the highest per-direction rate observed on this account, so
the estimate is an upper bound and the cap cannot fire late. Per UTC day:

    spend = max( sum over regions and the four token metrics of
                   undimensioned CloudWatch Sum * CEILING[metric],
                 ce_spend )

Cost Explorer stays in enforcement: it is the only signal covering Bedrock spend
publishing no token metric (Cohere Rerank is live; provisioned throughput, batch
and customization are structural), and it is orthogonal to all four defects.
CloudWatch reads move from per-ModelId enumeration to the four undimensioned
aggregates — verified equivalent 2026-09-14 to 09-24 to four decimal places.

**Release discriminator.** An all-empty CloudWatch read is ambiguous: it is both a
metrics-delivery gap and the normal idle/new-UTC-day state on which the automatic
release depends. Empty is therefore never treated as unavailable on its own. The
cap may release on an empty read only when CE for that day is available and zero;
if CE is nonzero or unavailable, the deny is held.

### Accepted limitation

Ceiling pricing over-estimates for models much cheaper than the priciest. The
cheapest here are two orders of magnitude below, and two models currently bill
nothing for cache-write, so the factor is unbounded: a large embedding or
small-model batch job can trip the cap at a small fraction of intended spend.
Accepted for simplicity. The remedy if it bites is an exact-match
`{ModelId: rate}` override defaulting to the ceiling — equality only, never
substring or normalisation, so it cannot reopen this class.

## Figures

Machine-local policy bars spend totals, unit costs, budgets, cap thresholds and
bill figures from the tracker, because the tickets branch auto-pushes to the
public GitHub mirror. The same bar applies to anything committed to the code
repo, which is also public. Constants, threshold, observed rates, back-test
distribution and incident figures are in the operator's local-only note
`~/Desktop/bedrock-cap-redesign-local-only/design.md`. Implement from that file;
copy no figure into this ticket, a comment, a session log, a commit or the repo.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The seven pricing functions (`_refresh_rates`, `_rate_for`, `_seed_for`,
  `_normalise`, `_strip_billing_region`, `_marketplace_rate_key`,
  `_rate_key_for_ce_group`) and six constants (`SEED_RATES`, `RATE_OVERRIDES`,
  `BEDROCK_SERVICE_VALUES`, `MARKETPLACE_TOKEN_SUFFIXES`, `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K`,
  `MARKETPLACE_TOKENS_PER_RATE_UNIT`) are absent from the module. Checked: a test
  asserting none of those names survives.
- [ ] The `TOKEN_METRICS` direction multipliers are removed. Checked: the same test.
- [ ] `_metered_spend` issues exactly four undimensioned `GetMetricData` queries
  per region and calls no `list_metrics` on the enforcement path. Checked: a test
  asserting the stubbed client recorded four queries per region, zero
  `list_metrics`.
- [ ] A `CEILING` mapping gives one rate per token metric, each at least the
  highest rate for that direction in the fixture. Checked: a test deriving
  observed rates from the fixture and comparing.
- [ ] Enforcement compares `max(ceiling_estimate, ce_spend)` against the
  threshold. Checked: a test driving each arm larger in turn.
- [ ] `_ce_spend_today` classifies Bedrock spend by predicate (service equals
  `Amazon Bedrock` or ends with the Bedrock Edition suffix), not an allowlist.
  Checked: a test proving it matches every Bedrock service in the fixture,
  including the five the allowlist omitted.
- [ ] On an all-empty CloudWatch read the cap releases only when CE for that day
  is available and zero. Checked: two tests — empty read with CE zero releases;
  empty read with CE nonzero holds.
- [ ] On an all-empty CloudWatch read with CE unavailable, the deny is held.
  Checked: a test stubbing a CE exception.
- [ ] Any exception from a metered or CE read fails closed: no release, deny
  unchanged. Checked: a test raising from each client in turn.
- [ ] `infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf` carries the updated threshold and
  warning values from the design note. Checked: `terraform plan`.
- [ ] The now-orphaned `SEED_RATES`, `RATE_OVERRIDES`, `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K` and
  `RATE_WINDOW_DAYS` Lambda `environment` entries are deleted, together with
  `variable "bedrock_cap_seed_rates"`, `variable "bedrock_cap_unknown_rate_per_1k"`
  and the `bedrock_cap_seed_rates` / `bedrock_cap_rate_overrides` locals. Checked:
  `terraform plan` shows exactly those deletions plus the threshold and warning
  changes, and `terraform validate` passes with no unused declarations.
- [ ] `state["rates"]`, `state["rates_day"]`, `metered_estimated`, `MeteredRate`
  and the `" (estimated)"` rendering are removed. Checked: a test asserting the
  persisted state carries no rate table.
- [ ] A daily guard compares the ceiling estimate for a settled day against CE for
  that day and raises an SNS warning when the estimate is below actual. Checked: a
  test driving an invariant violation.
- [ ] That guard cannot attach or detach the policy. Checked: the same test
  asserting no IAM call.
- [ ] A daily `list_metrics` ModelId diff warns on a ModelId outside the recorded
  known set. Checked: a test adding an unknown ModelId to the fixture.
- [ ] Per-model token counts are logged on the warn and trip paths only, with no
  prices and no matching. Checked: a test asserting the line on trip and its
  absence on a normal tick.
- [ ] Tests run off committed CE and `list_metrics` fixtures whose structure is
  recorded from this account but whose dollar amounts and usage quantities are
  replaced with synthetic values, since the code repo is public. The CE fixture
  retains CamelCase, snake_case, `_Global` and a non-token usage type. Checked: a
  test asserting every ModelId in the `list_metrics` fixture is priced by the
  ceiling with no fallback path.
- [ ] The README's "How spend is measured" section no longer describes
  bill-derived rates, the seed fallback order or `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K`. Checked:
  a test asserting those strings are absent from the README.
- [ ] The README states the accepted over-estimate, the effective-cap band
  qualitatively, and that the figure is an upper bound rather than actual spend.
  Checked: reading the rendered section.

## Testing

- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py -q`
  proves every criterion above that names a test.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `make typecheck` are the commit gate.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make verify` before push, per AGENTS.md.
- `python3 scripts/terraform_prod.py plan --out <scratch>/plan.tfplan` must show
  exactly the env deltas named above before any apply.

## Rollback

This is a destructive cutover of a live safety control, so the back-out is
explicit. Immediate mitigation if the new expression misbehaves: set `DRY_RUN=true`
on the function, which stops it attaching or detaching while leaving it observable.
Full back-out: revert the Gerrit change and re-run the mediated
`scripts/terraform_prod.py` plan and apply. Terraform packages the handler by
content hash, so the revert restores the previous code and env exactly; the
deleted state keys are rebuilt on the next tick because the old code refreshes
them when absent.

## Out of scope

SSM write concurrency and the `signal_unavailable` deadlock: fourteen days of logs
show zero occurrences of either.
